chunks: And by this chain, he said:
The water of the well is vast; nothing would pollute it except if it is changed by it (the filth).

key_terms.مَاءُ الْبِئْرِ: Well water — the specific category of water being ruled upon
key_terms.وَاسِعٌ: Vast/capacious — implying the presumptive purity of plentiful water
key_terms.يَتَغَيَّرَ: Changes/is altered — the threshold criterion for impurity: change in taste, smell, or color
key_terms.يُفْسِدُهُ: Corrupts/renders impure — technical fiqh term for najasah contamination

ai.seo_question: When does well water become impure in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: The Imam rules that well water is inherently purifying (tahir) and cannot be rendered impure simply by contact with a pollutant. The water only becomes impure when its smell, color, or taste is visibly altered by the najasah (ritual impurity). This principle of presumed purity for large or flowing water bodies was a foundational ruling in early Shia jurisprudence, reflecting the practical circumstances of communities relying on wells for ritual purification.

en.hubeali: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water of the large well, nothing would pollute it except if it is changed by it (the filth)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Through the same chain of narrators as the previous Hadith the following is stated: “He (the Imam) ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘
Well water is vast. It does not become polluted until it is changed.’”
